reasons: The excerpt explicitly says to click Recordings and says recordings of site users can provide insight.
The listed filtering dimensions and example user-action filters directly match the excerpt.
Reviewing recordings is a reasonable dependency for filtering recordings.
The excerpt specifically recommends sorting clicks and pages both high-to-low and low-to-high to compare very active and less active users.
Reviewing recordings is a reasonable dependency for sorting them.
The action preserves the stated distinction: skip inactivity can help obtain quick insight, while first-time viewers or people new to Clarity can leave it off to see periods without movement.
The long-recording and first-time/new-user conditions are both grounded in the excerpt.
The excerpt presents a sticky filter as a possible improvement ('could very much be sticky'), not an unqualified required remedy; retain that conditional framing.

The asserted dependency on the separate generic 'Look for common navigation and click patterns' task is not stated as a prerequisite. The source ties this particular suggestion to observing users repeatedly return to the top, which is already captured by the candidate trigger.
Fixing the cart-removal usability issue is supported, including the urgency of fixing it.

The trigger incorrectly turns one illustrative recording outcome—one user leaving after 21 minutes—into a prerequisite. The source identifies the underlying menu-switch/cart-loss behavior as the problem to fix; it does not require observing that precise duration or departure scenario.
The excerpt directly recommends removing distractions for one to two hours, focusing on recordings, and repeatedly asking why users acted as they did.
The excerpt explicitly rejects a fixed recording count and says to continue until the main patterns, issues, and friction points are understood, after which further viewing becomes repetitive.
The completion condition accurately reflects the stated stopping point for that review cycle.
